name: Town Center and Market
tagline: Hsipaw's walkable core around the clock tower and morning market
description: The commercial heart of town, centered on the clock tower, main market street, and the busy morning market where Shan farmers and traders sell produce, noodles, and tea. Most guesthouses, trekking offices, banks (when functioning), and traveler cafes cluster here. It is the natural base for arrivals, entirely walkable, and the easiest place to arrange treks or transport onward.
bestFor: first-time visitors, trekkers arranging guides, budget travelers
pros: easiest place to book treks and transport
cons: can feel dusty and congested on market days

name: Shan Palace and Little Bagan Area
tagline: Historic royal grounds and a cluster of old stupas near the river
description: Home to the Shan Palace (the 'East Haw'), former seat of the Shan princely state, and a nearby cluster of aging brick stupas locally nicknamed 'Little Bagan'. Quieter and more residential than the market center, with a slower pace and a sense of Hsipaw's royal history. A short walk or bike ride from downtown, it rewards visitors interested in local heritage over amenities.
pros: peaceful compared to the market area
cons: few dining or shopping options nearby
palace visiting hours and access have been inconsistent

name: Dokhtawady Riverside
tagline: The river that runs along Hsipaw's edge, popular for sunset walks and swimming
description: The Dokhtawady (Myitnge) river skirts the eastern edge of town, with paths and small guesthouses set up for quiet walks, sunset views, and a swim in the dry season. It has a more relaxed, semi-rural feel than the market center while still being a short walk from downtown. A handful of riverside guesthouses offer some of the more scenic (if still basic) accommodation in town.
bestFor: travelers wanting quiet accommodation, sunset watchers
cons: fewer dining options within immediate reach
some paths and areas can flood or wash out in monsoon

name: Namhsan and Palaung Hill Trekking Area
tagline: The tea-growing highlands and Palaung villages northwest of Hsipaw
description: The hill country toward Namhsan, a Palaung town famed for tea cultivation, forms the classic multi-day trekking route out of Hsipaw, passing Shan and Palaung villages, tea plantations, and forested ridgelines. Visited via guided trek rather than as a base to stay in, it is where Hsipaw's reputation as a trekking hub actually plays out, though route access depends on current security conditions and should be confirmed with local guides before setting out.
bestFor: trekkers, travelers interested in hill-tribe culture
pros: authentic village homestays with local guides
far fewer tourists than Myanmar's headline sites
cons: access and safety conditions can change with little notice
basic homestay facilities, no independent travel without a guide
